name: Redguard
summary: The people of Hammerfell, descended from the Yokudans who crossed the sea. Born athletes and the finest swordsmen in Tamriel.

name: Orsimer
summary: The Orcs, children of Malacath, living in strongholds across the north. Superb smiths and heavy-armoured fighters, long scorned by the other races.

name: Nord
summary: The tall, fair people of Skyrim, hardened by its cold. Fierce warriors and seafarers who prize courage, mead and the Voice of their ancestors.

name: Khajiit
summary: The cat-folk of Elsweyr. Their shape depends on the phases of the moons at birth, from the near-human Ohmes to the great Senche. Quick, agile and fond of moon sugar.

name: Imperial
summary: The people of Cyrodiil, heart of the Empire. Diplomats, traders and soldiers of the Legion, known for their discipline and silver tongues.

name: Dunmer
summary: The Dark Elves of Morrowind: grey-skinned, red-eyed, fire-blooded. Ruled by Great Houses and the Tribunal Temple, wary of outsiders.

name: Breton
summary: The people of High Rock, mixed Nedic and Elven blood. Born with a feel for magic and a natural resistance to it; their kingdoms quarrel endlessly.

name: Bosmer
summary: The Wood Elves of Valenwood: quick, nimble and the best archers in Tamriel. Their Green Pact forbids harming the forest, so they eat only meat.

name: Argonian
summary: The scaled people of Black Marsh, bound to the Hist trees of their homeland. Breathe water, shrug off disease, and are rarely trusted by the Dunmer next door.

name: Altmer
summary: The High Elves of the Summerset Isles: tall, golden-skinned and proud of the oldest Aldmeri blood. Gifted mages, often thought aloof by the other races.

name: The Warrior
summary: Guardian sign of Last Seed, protector of the Lady, Steed and Lord. Its children are held to be quick-tempered and handy with weapons.

name: The Mage
summary: Guardian sign of Rain's Hand, protector of the Apprentice, Atronach and Ritual. Its children are gifted casters, but said to be proud and forgetful.

name: The Thief
summary: Guardian sign of Evening Star, protector of the Lover, Shadow and Tower. Its children court danger and dodge it, until their luck runs dry.

name: The Lady
summary: Charge of the Warrior, rising in Hearthfire. Those born under her are thought to be gentle and forgiving.

name: The Steed
summary: Charge of the Warrior, rising in Midyear. Its children are said to be restless and always in a hurry to be elsewhere.

name: The Lord
summary: Charge of the Warrior, rising in First Seed. Its children are thought hardy and healthy; some call them Trollkin for a weakness to fire.

name: The Apprentice
summary: Charge of the Mage, rising in Sun's Height. Its children take to magic easily, yet magic also bites them harder.

name: The Atronach
summary: Charge of the Mage, rising in Sun's Dusk. Its children hold deep wells of magicka but cannot refill them on their own.

name: The Ritual
summary: Charge of the Mage, rising in Morning Star. Its gifts are said to shift with the moons and planets; often linked with healing and mending.

name: The Lover
summary: Charge of the Thief, rising in Sun's Dawn. Those born under it are thought graceful and full of passion.

name: The Shadow
summary: Charge of the Thief, rising in Second Seed. Its children are said to slip into darkness and go unseen.

name: The Tower
summary: Charge of the Thief, rising in Frostfall. Its children are said to sniff out gold and get past any lock.

name: The Serpent
summary: The thirteenth sign: belongs to no season and no guardian, drifting across the sky. Its children are both the most blessed and the most cursed.

name: Acrobat
summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Endurance. A nimble type who trusts agility and stamina and does not fear a long leap.

name: Agent
summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Personality. Smooth talker in company, hard to spot once out of the light.

name: Archer
summary: Combat specialization; favoured Agility, Strength. Fights from range and aims to drop a foe before blades are drawn.

name: Assassin
summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Intelligence, Speed. Quiet and quick, strikes the unaware from the dark; locks rarely stop them.

name: Barbarian
summary: Combat specialization; favoured Speed, Strength. Fast, brutal fighter who skips heavy plate and simply overpowers the enemy.

name: Bard
summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Intelligence, Personality. Sharp and sociable; tries words first and the sword second.

name: Battlemage
summary: Magic specialization; favoured Intelligence, Strength. Half scholar, half soldier, equally ready with a spell or a weapon.

name: Crusader
summary: Combat specialization; favoured Strength, Willpower. Heavy hitter who patches their own wounds with restoration between fights.

name: Healer
summary: Magic specialization; favoured Personality, Willpower. Battles sickness and poison with restoration, and uses destruction when pressed.

name: Knight
summary: Combat specialization; favoured Personality, Strength. The noble fighter: strong of arm and of character.

name: Mage
summary: Magic specialization; favoured Intelligence, Willpower. Relies on broad magical learning, which they hold to be stronger than steel.

name: Monk
summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Willpower. Strong-willed and quick, fights with bare hands or the bow.

name: Nightblade
summary: Magic specialization; favoured Speed, Willpower. Moves fast through shadow and uses spells to tilt the odds.

name: Pilgrim
summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Endurance, Personality. Tough, well-read traveller who gets by through trade and persuasion.

name: Rogue
summary: Combat specialization; favoured Personality, Speed. Quick rather than strong, with a tongue as sharp as the blade.

name: Scout
summary: Combat specialization; favoured Endurance, Speed. Prefers the open country to town life; good at avoiding harm and guarding themselves.

name: Sorcerer
summary: Magic specialization; favoured Endurance, Intelligence. A caster tough enough to wear heavy armour while slinging spells.

name: Spellsword
summary: Magic specialization; favoured Endurance, Willpower. Blend of fighter and caster, more agile than a sorcerer and less predictable.

name: Thief
summary: Stealth specialization; favoured Agility, Speed. Lives off other people's losses: quick in the shadows, shrewd at the market.

name: Warrior
summary: Combat specialization; favoured Endurance, Strength. Melee generalist who charges in and has little use for magic.

name: Witchhunter
summary: Magic specialization; favoured Agility, Intelligence. Light on their feet and clever with spells, keeps foes at a distance with arrows.

name: Custom class (default name "Adventurer")
summary: Player-built class: pick a specialization, two favoured attributes and seven major skills. Oblivion names it Adventurer by default; any name allowed.

name: Cyrodiil
summary: Imperial heartland and seat of the Empire. In 3E 433 the Emperor is murdered and the Ruby Throne left empty; ruled meanwhile by Chancellor Ocato and the Elder Council.

name: Black Marsh
summary: Argonian swamp province in the southeast. An Imperial province in 3E 433, recently at war with its Dunmer neighbours (Arnesian War).

name: Elsweyr
summary: Khajiit province of deserts and jungles. In the late 3E a confederacy within the Empire, prospering on moon sugar trade and feuding with Leyawiin at the border.

name: Hammerfell
summary: Redguard desert province in the west. Part of the Empire in 3E 433; it later walks away from the Empire after the Great War of 4E 171 to 175.

name: High Rock
summary: Breton province of rival kingdoms around the Iliac Bay. Loyal to the Empire in 3E 433; its map was redrawn by the Warp in the West of 3E 417.

name: Morrowind
summary: Dunmer homeland. In 3E 433 an Imperial province with wide autonomy under the Armistice; its gods are gone or missing after 3E 427, but the Red Year has not happened yet.

name: Skyrim
summary: Cold northern Nord province. Part of the Empire in 3E 433, the year its Nords take all of Solstheim.

name: Summerset Isles
summary: Altmer island province in the southwest. In 3E 433 still ruled by its old monarchy inside the Empire; renamed Alinor only after the Thalmor coup of 4E 22.

name: Valenwood
summary: Bosmer forest province in the southwest. Part of the Empire in 3E 433 with an Empire-friendly government until the Thalmor-backed coup of 4E 29.

name: Orsinium (Orc kingdom, not a province)
summary: Orc city-state between Wayrest and the Wrothgarian Mountains, refounded by Gortwog in 3E 399. Its bid to become a full province was still under review in 3E 433.

name: Heartlands
summary: Central grassy lowland around Lake Rumare and the Upper Niben, with the Imperial City at its heart.

name: Great Forest
summary: Huge crescent of woodland wrapping round the Heartlands on three sides; Chorrol lies on its edge.

name: Colovian Highlands
summary: Hilly, wooded far west of Cyrodiil, remote from Imperial centres and known for strong red wine.

name: Gold Coast
summary: Cyrodiil's western coastline between the Brena and the Strid; home of the port of Anvil and of Kvatch.

name: West Weald
summary: Open Colovian countryside in the southwest, famous for vineyards and tomatoes; Skingrad is its city.

name: Jerall Mountains
summary: Snowy northern range on the Skyrim border; Bruma and Cloud Ruler Temple sit here.

name: Nibenay Basin
summary: Eastern farmland of the Niben valley, heartland of the Nibenese; Cheydinhal lies near its eastern hills.

name: Nibenay Valley
summary: Humid, river-cut south of the Niben running down to Niben Bay; Bravil is its city.

name: Blackwood
summary: Swampy far south around Leyawiin, bordering Black Marsh and draining into Topal Bay.

name: Valus Mountains
summary: Eastern range on the Morrowind border, meeting the Jeralls and Velothi range at Mount Trolhetta.

name: Imperial City
summary: Capital of Cyrodiil and the Empire on City Isle in Lake Rumare; its Temple of the One honours Akatosh.

name: Anvil
summary: Port city of the far southwest; patron Dibella; notable Redguard and Bosmer residents.

name: Bravil
summary: Damp river town on Niben Bay, called the poorest in Cyrodiil; patron Mara.

name: Bruma
summary: Snowbound northern city with many Nords; patron Talos.

name: Cheydinhal
summary: Northeastern city with many Dunmer and Orcs; patron Arkay.

name: Chorrol
summary: Northwestern city at the edge of the Great Forest; patron Stendarr.

name: Kvatch
summary: Hill city of Akatosh, overrun and burned by Daedra from the first Oblivion Gate in 3E 433. A "Kvatch refugee" is a strong era origin.

name: Leyawiin
summary: Southern city near Black Marsh and Elsweyr with many Argonians and Khajiit; patron Zenithar.

name: Skingrad
summary: Wine city of the southwest, split into two districts by bridges; patron Julianos.

name: Arboretum
summary: Imperial City district. Park district of statues and trees.

name: Elven Gardens District
summary: Imperial City district. Residential quarter in the northwest of the city.

name: Market District
summary: Imperial City district. Commercial quarter with most shops and services.

name: Talos Plaza District
summary: Imperial City district. Well-off residential quarter with a dragon statue at its centre.

name: Temple District
summary: Imperial City district. Residential quarter around the Temple of the One.

name: Waterfront District
summary: Imperial City district. The docks on City Isle's southwest shore; poor, and home turf of the Thieves Guild.

name: Arena District
summary: Imperial City district. Eastern quarter built around the Arena.

name: Green Emperor Way
summary: Imperial City district. Cemetery and gardens at the core, around the Imperial Palace.

name: Aleswell
summary: Roadside village whose folk are said to have vanished; rumoured haunted until its quest is solved.

name: Blankenmarch
summary: Tiny hamlet of three houses and a garden in the south.

name: Bleaker's Way
summary: Village founded by Ulf the Bleaker; run by the rival Ulfgar and Dalvilu families.

name: Border Watch
summary: Khajiit village near Elsweyr, built in Leyawiin style, bound to the K'Sharra Prophecy.

name: Brindle Home
summary: Small village where one resident has angered a Daedric Prince.

name: Cropsford
summary: Village wrecked by two feuding goblin tribes and rebuilt with outside help.

name: Hackdirt
summary: Mining village with a dark cult secret; very hostile to outsiders.

name: Harlun's Watch
summary: Quiet village troubled by strange lights from a nearby cave.

name: Pell's Gate
summary: Small Heartlands village, once home of the swordswoman known as Umbra.

name: Water's Edge
summary: Riverside hamlet near Leyawiin, massacred by the Blackwood Company during the Fighters Guild story.

name: Weye
summary: Tiny Heartlands hamlet: one house and the Wawnet Inn.

name: The Nine Divines (Imperial Cult, "the Chapel")
summary: State faith of the Empire: the Eight plus Talos. In Cyrodiil simply called the Church or Chapel; each city chapel honours one patron Divine.

name: Daedra worship
summary: Private devotion to a Daedric Prince at a shrine. Legal but frowned on; mainstream priests sometimes lead witch hunts against worshippers.

name: Tribunal Temple (Dunmer)
summary: Old faith of Morrowind in Almalexia, Sotha Sil and Vivec. By 3E 433 two are dead and Vivec is missing; the Temple is shaken but standing.

name: Racial and regional pantheons (pointer)
summary: Each culture has its own pantheon (Nordic, Yokudan, Khajiiti, Bosmeri, Hist, Orcish etc.). Covered per race by other research; see Lore:Religions.

name: Fighters Guild
summary: Chartered guild of hired swords with halls in every city. In 3E 433 led by Vilena Donton and under pressure from the Blackwood Company.

name: Associate
summary: Rank 1 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Apprentice
summary: Rank 2 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Journeyman
summary: Rank 3 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Swordsman
summary: Rank 4 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Protector
summary: Rank 5 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Defender
summary: Rank 6 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Warder
summary: Rank 7 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Guardian
summary: Rank 8 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Champion
summary: Rank 9 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Master
summary: Rank 10 of 10 in the Fighters Guild.

name: Mages Guild
summary: Guild of scholars and casters, centred on the Arcane University. Arch-Mage Hannibal Traven (chosen 3E 431) has banned necromancy.

name: Associate
summary: Rank 1 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Apprentice
summary: Rank 2 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Journeyman
summary: Rank 3 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Evoker
summary: Rank 4 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Conjurer
summary: Rank 5 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Magician
summary: Rank 6 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Warlock
summary: Rank 7 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Wizard
summary: Rank 8 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Master-Wizard
summary: Rank 9 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Arch-Mage
summary: Rank 10 of 10 in the Mages Guild.

name: Thieves Guild
summary: Outlawed but tolerated guild led by the Gray Fox. House rules: never steal from members, never kill on a job, never rob the poor.

name: Pickpocket
summary: Rank 1 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Footpad
summary: Rank 2 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Bandit
summary: Rank 3 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Prowler
summary: Rank 4 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Cat Burglar
summary: Rank 5 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Shadowfoot
summary: Rank 6 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Master Thief
summary: Rank 7 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Gray Fox
summary: Rank 8 of 8 in the Thieves Guild (the last is a unique title).

name: Dark Brotherhood
summary: Secret guild of assassins serving Sithis and the Night Mother, bound by the Five Tenets and run by the Black Hand.

name: Murderer
summary: Rank 1 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Slayer
summary: Rank 2 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Eliminator
summary: Rank 3 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Assassin
summary: Rank 4 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Executioner
summary: Rank 5 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Silencer
summary: Rank 6 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Speaker
summary: Rank 7 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Listener
summary: Rank 8 of 8 in the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Imperial Legion
summary: The Empire's army: garrisons forts, patrols roads and keeps the peace. Not joinable in Oblivion, but fine for RP backstory.

name: Emperor of Tamriel
summary: Head of the Empire. Uriel Septim VII is murdered in 3E 433; his hidden son Martin is the last Septim heir.

name: Alfiq
summary: Tiny four-legged furstock about the size of a housecat, without thumbs. Born when Masser wanes and Secunda is full.

name: Alfiq-raht
summary: Quadruped furstock a little bigger than the Alfiq; little else is recorded. Born when Masser wanes and Secunda waxes.

name: Cathay
summary: Upright, plantigrade, fully furred Khajiit of roughly Man or Mer size with a long tail. UESP captions an Oblivion Khajiit as Cathay. Born Masser waxing, Secunda full.

name: Cathay-raht
summary: A bigger, stronger Cathay, known as front-line infantry in the Five Year War with Valenwood. Born when both Masser and Secunda wax.

name: Dagi
summary: One of the smallest furstocks, with a lynx-like face. Born when Masser wanes and Secunda is new.

name: Dagi-raht
summary: Two-legged, lynx-faced furstock, slightly larger than the Dagi but still short. Born when both moons wane.

name: Ohmes
summary: Elf-like, furless biped who often paints a feline face; the Arena-era look. Born when Masser is new and Secunda full.

name: Ohmes-raht
summary: Human-built plantigrade biped with thin fur and a tail; the Daggerfall-era look. Born when Masser is new and Secunda waxes.

name: Pahmar
summary: Giant, tiger-like biped, smaller only than the Pahmar-raht. Born when Masser is full and Secunda new.

name: Pahmar-raht
summary: Very tall plantigrade giant that looks much like a senche-tiger on two legs. Born when Masser is full and Secunda wanes.

name: Senche
summary: Large four-legged furstock with tawny fur and blood-red stripes and an apelike build. Born when both moons are full.

name: Senche-raht
summary: The largest furstock, a quadruped nicknamed the battlecat, said to be the longest-lived. Born when Masser is full and Secunda waxes.

name: Suthay
summary: Digitigrade biped, shorter than the Suthay-raht. Born when both moons are new.

name: Suthay-raht
summary: Man-height digitigrade biped with full fur, tail and cat head; the Morrowind and Redguard look. Born when Masser is new and Secunda wanes.

name: Tojay
summary: Little-known furstock said to resemble the Cathay; sources disagree on its leg type. Born when Masser waxes and Secunda is new.

name: Tojay-raht
summary: Digitigrade biped, larger than the Tojay. Born when Masser waxes and Secunda wanes.

name: Mane
summary: Unique Khajiit born only when Masser and Secunda align. Tradition holds a single Mane lives at a time and is reborn. Not a player option.

name: Anequina
summary: Arid northern half of Elsweyr, named for the warrior clan Ne Quin-al. Also an Oblivion Remastered Origin with the old male stat spread.

name: Pellitine
summary: Lush southern half of Elsweyr with jungles, rivers and beaches, rich from sugar and saltrice. Also an Oblivion Remastered Origin (old female stats).

name: High Savannah
summary: Northern grassland of Anequina around Riverhold.

name: The Scar
summary: Great canyon of northern Elsweyr that winds around the mesa city of Orcrest.

name: The Rim
summary: Northeastern borderland near Cyrodiil whose chief city is Rimmen.

name: Tenmar Forest
summary: Southern jungle where moon sugar is native and where Torval stands.

name: Quin'rawl Peninsula
summary: Southeastern peninsula between Topal Bay and the Southern Sea, home of the port of Senchal.

name: Khenarthi's Roost
summary: Island in the Southern Sea shared by Khajiit and Maormer, with moon sugar plantations.

name: Reaper's March
summary: Contested borderland between Elsweyr and Valenwood, partly Khajiiti, near Dune.

name: Trans-Niben (disputed)
summary: Land between Elsweyr and Black Marsh handed back to County Leyawiin by the Mane ca. 3E 432; Khajiit radicals still claim it.

name: Torval
summary: Jungle city near Valenwood and seat of the Mane. An active city-state under King Mojtabe ca. 3E 389 to 399.

name: Senchal
summary: Huge southern port long known for pirates, thieves and skooma, later a resort for rich Khajiit. Had its own king in the late Third Era.

name: Rimmen
summary: Walled resort city near the Cyrodiil border, often called Anequina's capital. Wealthy under King Ommed in the late Third Era.

name: Dune
summary: Hilltop merchant town by Reaper's March, home of the Temple of Two-Moons Dance where would-be Manes finish their path.

name: Orcrest
summary: Walled city perched on a plateau inside the Scar, reached by a large stone bridge.

name: Riverhold
summary: River crossroads and trading post on the northern border; Ta'agra name Rawla-Kei.

name: Corinthe
summary: Highland city in the heart of the province at the edge of the Tenmar Forest, once an ancient kingdom.

name: Ne Quin-al (old capital)
summary: Former Anequinan capital with a Temple of Two-Moons Dance, taken by rebels in 2E 326. Use as ancestral flavor only.

name: Northern nomads
summary: Tribes and prides of the dry north who keep roaming ways; raiders sometimes rally under one chieftain.

name: Southern city dwellers
summary: Settled, mercantile southerners with a plantation aristocracy and strong arts, quick to adopt Imperial ways by the late Third Era.

name: Ta'agra
summary: Khajiiti language. Most natives also speak Tamrielic with their own dialect and drop Ta'agra words into it. 'Khajiit' roughly means desert-walker.

name: Claw-Dances
summary: Khajiiti unarmored martial arts, called Rain-of-Sand styles by outsiders, practiced as moving meditation in temples and adeptoriums.

name: Moon sugar and skooma
summary: Sacred crystal seen as solid moonlight, used as spice, ritual sacrament and drug. Illegal in the Third Empire and widely smuggled; skooma is its stronger form.

name: Clan Mother
summary: Matriarchs widely seen as the strongest force in Khajiit society because they control moon sugar harvest and refining.

name: Moon-Singer
summary: Respected lore-keepers and storytellers, mostly in Elsweyr; some tales are split across several singers to protect them.

name: Ne Quin-al clan
summary: Ancient warrior clan skilled in war and tactics whose name became Anequina; kept nomadic customs in the north.

name: Pa'alatiin clan
summary: Ancient Moon-Priest clan that lived among all others and gave Pellitine its name; settled the south.

name: Duneguard Outwalkers
summary: Brigand clan, once the Dakarn Clan, that fought Valenwood's rangers in Reaper's March.

name: Riddle'Thar (Two-Moons Dance)
summary: Mainstream Khajiiti faith, more a code for living than one god, revealed by the prophet-Mane Rid-Thar-ri'Datta. Promises the paradise Llesw'er.

name: The Hist
summary: Sentient spore trees joined by one root mind. Their sap shapes hatchlings, gives names and visions, and souls return to them at death.

name: Sithis (Argonian view)
summary: Revered as the force of change, not pure ruin. Argonians rebuild rather than mourn. Differs from the Dark Brotherhood's Sithis.

name: Green Pact (Treaty of Frond and Leaf)
summary: Y'ffre's covenant: guard the forest, eat only meat, waste nothing, eat slain foes within three days, keep the form Y'ffre gave. Fallen fruit and honey are usually fine.

name: Bosmeri Eight
summary: Y'ffre, Auri-El (little honored), Arkay, Xarxes, Mara, Stendarr, Z'en and Baan Dar. Hircine and the Wilderking also loom in folk belief.

name: The Ooze
summary: The formless chaos before Y'ffre named the world. Pact-breakers are said to return to it after death.

name: The Silvenar
summary: Spiritual Voice of the People who embodies the Pact. Chosen by the Green, not by vote. Not a player title.

name: The Green Lady
summary: The Silvenar's partner and the physical face of the people, bound to the Silvenar in the generational Handfasting. Not a player title.

name: Treethane
summary: Local Bosmer leader with widely varying authority, part of Valenwood's loose patchwork rule. Some enforce the Pact.

name: Spinner
summary: Priest of Y'ffre who keeps stories and laws and enforces the Pact. Often said to hold the real power in Valenwood.

name: Jaqspur
summary: Earned title for elite long-range archers with a fast snatch-and-release draw. Work as scouts, trackers, hunters and guards.

name: Aldmeri pantheon
summary: Ancestor-gods led by Auri-El: Magnus, Trinimac, Jephre, Xarxes, Mara, Stendarr, Syrabane, plus Phynaster. Traditionalists reject a fixed count of Eight.

name: Altmeri monarch
summary: Summerset's crown at Alinor, under Imperial rule in 3E 433. City kings such as Skywatch's also exist. Not a player title.

name: Sapiarch
summary: Scholar of the College of Sapiarchs; each studies one field and they tutor royal heirs.

name: Cheydinhal (Cyrodiil)
summary: Eastern Cyrodiil town with Dunmer-style architecture and a Dunmer Count, Andel Indarys. Main home of Dark Elves in Cyrodiil.

name: House Dunmer (settled)
summary: Dark Elves of the towns and plantations, sworn to or living under a Great House and the Temple.

name: Ashlander
summary: Nomadic Dunmer of the wastes who keep the old ancestor and Daedra faith and reject the Tribunal. Wary of outlanders.

name: Velothi
summary: Ashlander-descended Dunmer who settled among the Great Houses.

name: Cyrodiil Dunmer (diaspora)
summary: Dark Elves living in Cyrodiil, centered on Cheydinhal, an early wave of the Dunmer diaspora.

name: Chimer ancestry
summary: Golden-skinned forebears who left Summerset with Veloth and were cursed by Azura into Dunmer after Red Mountain. Ancestry only.

name: House Redoran
summary: Warrior house of duty and honor, seated at Ald'ruhn and the most powerful house of recent centuries. Supplies many Buoyant Armigers.

name: House Hlaalu
summary: Merchant house friendliest to the Empire, seated at Balmora, leading under King Helseth. Tainted by Camonna Tong links.

name: House Telvanni
summary: Isolationist wizard-lords in mushroom towers, seated at Sadrith Mora and Port Telvannis. Power through magic, little law.

name: House Indoril
summary: Orthodox house bound to the Temple and hostile to the Empire, holding Mournhold. Lost its lead on the Council at the Armistice.

name: House Dres
summary: Agrarian slaver house of the south, seated at Tear. Clung to slavery long after others moved on.

name: House Dagoth (Sixth House)
summary: Lost house destroyed after Red Mountain; its lord Dagoth Ur fell in 3E 427. Membership in 3E 433 means a hunted cultist.

name: Great House ranks
summary: Hlaalu/Redoran: Hireling, Retainer, Oathman, Lawman, Kinsman, House Cousin, House Brother, House Father, Councilman. Telvanni: Mouth, Spellwright, Wizard, Master, Magister.

name: Councilor / Hortator
summary: House councilors sit on the Grand Council; in grave danger they may elect a Hortator as war leader.

name: Archmagister / Archmaster / Grandmaster
summary: Top ranks of Telvanni, Redoran and Hlaalu respectively. Not a player title.

name: King of Morrowind
summary: Helseth reigns from Mournhold under the Empire and banned slavery late in the era. Not a player title.

name: Urshilaku
summary: Ashlander tribe of the Ashlands and West Gash, most devoted to the Nerevarine prophecies.

name: Ahemmusa
summary: Ashlander tribe of Azura's Coast.

name: Erabenimsun
summary: Ashlander tribe of Molag Amur.

name: Zainab
summary: Ashlander tribe of the Grazelands.

name: Mainland tribes (Kagesh, Ulath, Vereansu)
summary: Ashlander tribes of Stonefalls and Deshaan.

name: Mabrigash
summary: Ashlander witch-warrior cult of the Ghost Snake, founded by Farseer Hareth.

name: Tribunal Temple
summary: State church of Almalexia, Sotha Sil and Vivec (ALMSIVI). In 3E 433 shaken: the gods lost their divine source in 3E 427 and are dead or missing.

name: Ancestor worship
summary: Core of all Dunmer religion: family spirits guard the household and tomb. Daedra are counted as ancestors too.

name: Good Daedra (Azura, Boethiah, Mephala)
summary: The Chimer's old gods. Under the Temple called the Anticipations; Ashlanders worship them directly.

name: House of Troubles
summary: Mehrunes Dagon, Sheogorath, Malacath and Molag Bal, seen as gods who test the Dunmer.

name: Nerevarine cult
summary: Urshilaku-rooted belief in Nerevar reborn as an outlander. The prophecy was fulfilled in 3E 427.

name: Slavery
summary: Long protected Dunmer custom targeting Argonians and Khajiit, banned by King Helseth late in the Third Era amid violent backlash.

name: Trinimac cult
summary: Orcs who hold that Trinimac still lives and Malacath is a deceiver. Gortwog founded a priesthood; most Orcs call it heresy.

name: King / Queen
summary: Rulers of Redguard city-kingdoms, e.g. King Lhotun of Sentinel and Queen Clavilla of Taneth. Not for player cards without admin approval.

name: Baron / Baroness
summary: Lord of a Hammerfell barony such as Bergama or Kozanset.

name: High Prophet
summary: Religious-political leader title held by Ayaan-si of Elinhir, voice of the Crown revolt against Sentinel.

name: Yokudan pantheon
summary: The old Redguard gods (Satakal, Ruptga, Tu'whacca, Morwha, Zeht, Tava, Onsi, Leki and others). Core faith of the Crowns and desert tribes.

name: Divines (Forebear practice)
summary: Forebears largely follow the Imperial Divines, sometimes under Yokudan names (Tu'whacca for Arkay, Zeht for Zenithar). Crowns see this as betrayal.

name: Ancestor reverence
summary: Redguards honor their dead intensely; corpses are sacred, mummification is practiced and disturbing a tomb is sacrilege.

name: Colovian
summary: Western Imperials: frontier folk with strong Nordic roots, plain or martial in dress, devout to the Divines, and the backbone of the Legion.

name: Nibenese
summary: Eastern Imperials of the Niben valley: showy dress, tattoos and brands, cults and ceremony, a battlemage aristocracy. Seen as the high culture of Cyrodiil.

name: Heartlander
summary: Nibenese subculture around the Imperial City; secular-leaning, treating faith as a private matter.

name: Nibenese tattoos
summary: Tattoos and brandings that mark a Nibenese person's faith, political faction or way of life.

name: Nedic ancestry
summary: Pre-Imperial human peoples of Tamriel. The Nibenese are described as the closest living thing to pure Nedes.

name: Kothringi (not Imperial)
summary: Silver-skinned human tribe of Black Marsh, probably Nedic, wiped out by the Knahaten Flu. Not Imperials; ancestry only, with an explicit lore caveat.

name: Colovia (Colovian West)
summary: Western Cyrodiil: Gold Coast, West Weald, Colovian Highlands, Great Forest. Core counties Anvil, Chorrol, Kvatch, Skingrad.

name: Nibenay (Nibenean East)
summary: Eastern Cyrodiil along the Niben: counties Bravil, Bruma, Cheydinhal, Leyawiin, plus the Heartlands around City Isle.

name: Heartlands
summary: Central lands around Lake Rumare and the Imperial City.

name: Imperial City
summary: Capital of the Empire on City Isle; Nibenese in style, with Ayleid walls and White-Gold Tower. Seat of the Elder Council.

name: Anvil
summary: Colovian port county on the Gold Coast.

name: Kvatch
summary: Hilltop Colovian county on the Gold Coast, sacked by Daedra early in the Oblivion Crisis. Strong hook for refugee characters.

name: Skingrad
summary: Colovian county in the West Weald, known for wine.

name: Chorrol
summary: Main town of the Colovian Highlands.

name: Bruma
summary: Jerall Mountains county, Nibenese in custom but mostly Nord in people and building. Holds the Great Chapel of Talos; besieged by Daedra in 3E 433.

name: Cheydinhal
summary: Nibenese county by the Valus Mountains with Dunmeri touches in its architecture.

name: Bravil
summary: Nibenese county on Niben Bay in the Nibenay Valley.

name: Leyawiin
summary: Southern Nibenese county, roughly the same as the Blackwood region.

name: Septim Dynasty
summary: Ruling imperial line. Uriel VII and his known heirs are murdered in 3E 433; Martin dies ending the Crisis. Claiming Septim blood should be admin-only.

name: Emperor
summary: Ruler of Tamriel from the Ruby Throne; Uriel Septim VII until his murder in 3E 433. Not a player title.

name: Count / Countess
summary: Ruler of a Cyrodiil county such as Anvil or Skingrad (e.g. Count Marius Caro). Lesser nobles may use Lord or Lady.

name: Nine Divines
summary: Akatosh, Arkay, Dibella, Julianos, Kynareth, Mara, Stendarr, Zenithar and Talos. State faith of the Empire; Talos worship is lawful in 3E 433.

name: Nibenese cults
summary: Eastern devotions alongside the Divines: Ancestor-Moth, hero cults of Reman and Tiber Septim, animal and ancestor spirits.

name: King / Queen
summary: Rulers of the Breton kingdoms; their children are Princes and Princesses. Addressed as Your Majesty.

name: Duke / Duchess
summary: High noble ruler, addressed as Your Grace; e.g. Duke Senhyn of Camlorn.

name: Marquis, Count, Viscount, Baron, Lord, Earl
summary: Lesser Breton ranks; barons often hold the title without land. Earls also appear (Jakben, Earl of Imbel).

name: Sir / Dame
summary: Address for knights of a Breton order. Orders once took only the high-born, later merchants too.

name: Eight and Nine Divines
summary: Most Bretons took up the Divines under the Alessian Empire; Daedra worship is generally frowned on.

name: Atmoran descent
summary: Nords trace their blood to Atmora, the frozen northern continent they left in waves; Ysgramor is the model ancestor.

name: Descent from Ysgramor's Five Hundred
summary: Family claim to one of the Five Hundred Companions who came with Ysgramor. A boast, not provable.

name: Skaal
summary: Nord offshoot tribe of northeast Solstheim; hospitable, nature-revering, worshipping the All-Maker instead of the Nordic gods.

name: Bruma Nords (Cyrodiil)
summary: Nord majority of Bruma in the Jerall Mountains; Nordic in building and faith but living under Nibenese law and custom.

name: High King / High Queen
summary: Ruler of all Skyrim, chosen by the jarls at the Moot. Not a player title.

name: Jarl
summary: Ruler of a hold. Named jarls for 3E 433 are not documented, so cards should not claim a specific seat.

name: Tongue (Thu'um user)
summary: Nord who can Shout, seen as Kyne's gift. Lore only; not a card option in OB:MP.

name: Nordic pantheon
summary: Old Nord gods led by Kyne, with Shor, Tsun, Stuhn, Mara, Dibella, Jhunal and Ysmir (Talos). Worshipped beside the Divines, including in Bruma.

name: All-Maker (Skaal faith)
summary: Skaal belief in a kind but unknowable creator and nature spirits, opposed by the Adversary in forms such as the Greedy Man.

name: Temple ward
summary: Left at or taken in by a chapel of the Nine and brought up by its priests. Knows the liturgy, the healing rites and the charity rolls better than any family home.

name: Street orphan
summary: Grew up without parents in a city slum, begging, running errands and learning to steal. In Cyrodiil such children often fall in with the beggars who quietly serve the Thieves Guild.

name: Noble household
summary: Raised in a count's or lord's household with tutors, servants and court manners, but never quite in line for the title. Expected to marry well or serve the family name.

name: Farmstead
summary: Raised on a farm far from the walls, up before dawn for planting, herding and harvest. Knows weather, soil and livestock, and how thin a farm's margin is in a bad year.

name: Caravan life
summary: Grew up on the road with a trading caravan, moving goods between cities. Learned to haggle, mend wagons, read the road for bandits and sleep anywhere.

name: Legion family
summary: Child of a soldier, raised around garrison forts and drill yards. Moved with each posting and learned discipline, rank and the Legion's ways before learning a trade.

name: Sailor's family
summary: Raised in a port by a family that worked the ships, often waiting months for a parent to return. Knows knots, tides and the gossip of harbours from Anvil to the Iliac Bay.

name: Raised abroad
summary: Brought up in a province far from the family's homeland, among another people. Speaks with their accent and keeps their customs, and is seen as a foreigner by both sides.

name: Mixed household
summary: Child of parents from two different races. Lore holds that a child usually takes the mother's race, perhaps with a trace of the father, and grows up between two sets of customs.

name: Innkeeper's child
summary: Grew up behind the counter of a roadside inn or city tavern, serving travellers and hearing every rumour. Knows people, drink and when a brawl is about to start.

name: Mining camp
summary: Raised in a camp beside an iron or ore mine, where the work is dark, dangerous and badly paid. Grew up strong, wary of cave-ins and of whatever lives deeper in the tunnels.

name: Raised in the wilds
summary: Raised by a hunter or hermit in a remote cabin, far from towns and law. Learned to track, snare and forage, but finds crowds and city rules strange.

name: War refugee
summary: Family fled a war zone during the child's early years, such as the Arnesian War or the strife around the Iliac Bay before the Warp in the West. Grew up poor in a new land, starting over.

name: House Hlaalu family
summary: Raised in a Hlaalu household, where trade, deals and friendly ties with the Empire are the family business. Learned to bargain and to smile at outlanders.

name: House Redoran family
summary: Raised in a stern Redoran household that values duty, honour and the Temple. Taught to fight, to obey the councils and to keep a straight face in hard times.

name: Telvanni household
summary: Grew up in the service of a Telvanni wizard in a grown mushroom tower. Learned that power, magical power above all, sets your worth, and that rules are for the weak.

name: Ashlander tribe
summary: Raised among nomadic Ashlanders, living in yurts and following herds across the wastes. Honours ancestors and the wise women, and distrusts the Great Houses and the Empire.

name: Emigrant to Cyrodiil
summary: Raised in a Dunmer family that left Morrowind for Cyrodiil, likely Cheydinhal, where the Count himself is Dunmer. Keeps the old customs but grew up in Imperial streets.

name: Colovian family
summary: Raised in the hilly west of Cyrodiil in a plain, hard-working, devout household. Colovians prize martial skill, frugality and old tradition, and many sons and daughters join the Legion.

name: Nibenese family
summary: Raised in the eastern Niben valley, where people love bright clothes, tattoos, ceremony and philosophy. Grew up amid temple rites, bureaucracy and endless talk.

name: Imperial City born
summary: Born within the White-Gold walls and raised among its districts, markets and the Arena's roar. Proud of the capital and a little dismissive of the provinces.

name: Gold Coast trading family
summary: Raised in Anvil or Kvatch among merchants, sailors and vintners of the western coast. Grew up with the sea trade, foreign ships and Colovian pride.

name: Trading caravan
summary: Born to a wandering Khajiit caravan that trades across Tamriel. Grew up with tents, campfires, haggling and moon sugar tales, and is often watched closely by city guards.

name: Southern estate family
summary: Raised in the jungles and river basins of southern Elsweyr, on a family estate growing saltrice or moon sugar. Learned refined manners, old trade customs and estate life.

name: Northern nomad pride
summary: Raised in a nomadic pride on the dry northern plains of Elsweyr, where clans raid, herd and wander. Learned to fight, ride the dunes and follow a strong chief.

name: Raised by the Moon priests
summary: Raised in a temple of the Riddle'Thar and the moon faith, steeped in the Two-Moons Dance and the Mane's teachings. Learned riddles, rites and the Khajiit view of the gods.

name: Border-town raised
summary: Raised in a Cyrodiil town near Elsweyr, such as Leyawiin or Bravil, among Imperials who often distrust Khajiit. Learned Imperial ways and quick wits to survive suspicion.

name: Raised in a Hold city
summary: Grew up in the city seat of one of Skyrim's holds, under the eye of its jarl and in the shadow of the mead hall. Knows clan feuds, songs of old heroes and hard winters.

name: Northern coast village
summary: Raised in a fishing or whaling village on the icy Sea of Ghosts. Grew up hauling nets, braving storms and fearing what rises from the cold water.

name: Skaal village
summary: Raised among the Skaal of Solstheim, Nords who hold to the All-Maker and a simple life of hunting and fishing. Wary of the Empire and of outsiders' greed.

name: Nord of Bruma
summary: Born to Nord settlers in Bruma, high in the Jerall Mountains of Cyrodiil. Keeps Nord customs and mead halls, but grew up as an Imperial subject.

name: High nobility
summary: Born to a ruling house: a count's, king's or jarl's family. Holds land, rank and privilege, plus the duties and feuds that come with them.

name: Minor nobility
summary: Of a lesser noble or knightly family: a title and a coat of arms, but little land or money. Serves a greater lord to keep the family name up.

name: Landed gentry
summary: Owns an estate, vineyard or farmland worked by tenants, without a noble title. Comfortable, respected locally and keen to marry into nobility.

name: Wealthy merchant
summary: From a rich trading family whose wealth rivals the nobility. Has coin, contacts and ships or shops, but no birthright to rule.

name: Guild artisan
summary: A skilled crafter or guild member with a recognised trade and a place in town life. Owns tools, maybe a shop, and earns an honest living.

name: Free commoner
summary: An ordinary free subject of the Empire: labourer, shop clerk or townsfolk. No title, no master, and no safety net beyond family and friends.

name: Peasant
summary: Works someone else's land as a tenant farmer and owes rent, crops or labour to a lord. Common in High Rock and Skyrim, and in the Cyrodiil countryside.

name: Servant
summary: Works in someone's household as a maid, cook, valet or groom. Free and paid, but has little time or standing of their own.

name: Bonded labourer
summary: Bound by contract or debt to work for a master for a set time. Legally free, unlike a slave, but cannot leave until the debt is paid.

name: Slave
summary: Owned as property by a master. In 3E 433 only Morrowind still allows slavery; Argonians and Khajiit are the most common slaves there.

name: Freed slave
summary: Once a slave in Morrowind, now free by purchase, release or escape. Free in law outside Morrowind, but marked by the past and wary of slavers.

name: Outcast or exile
summary: Cast out by family, clan, house or homeland, for a crime, a feud or a forbidden belief. Belongs nowhere, owes no one and is trusted by few.

name: Clergy
summary: Ordained or vowed member of a temple or faith, such as the Nine Divines or the Tribunal Temple. Respected and protected, but bound by vows and duty.

name: Tribal clan member
summary: Belongs to a clan that lives outside Imperial class lines, like the Ashlanders, the Reachfolk or the Skaal. Rank comes from the clan, not from Imperial law.

name: Farmer
summary: Grew grain, vegetables or fruit and kept a few animals. Used to long days, hard labour and worrying about weather and raiders.

name: Fisher
summary: Fished rivers, lakes or coastal waters for a living and sold the catch at market. Knows boats, nets and the moods of the water.

name: Hunter
summary: Hunted deer, boar and other game for meat and hides. Good with a bow, patient and at home in the wilds.

name: Trapper
summary: Set snares and traps for fur-bearing animals and sold the pelts. Spent long seasons alone in forests and mountains.

name: Miner
summary: Dug iron, silver or other ore out of the earth in cramped, dangerous tunnels. Strong, used to dark and to the risk of collapse.

name: Blacksmith
summary: Worked a forge making tools, horseshoes and nails, and repairing anything iron. Strong arms, burned hands and an eye for good metal.

name: Armorer
summary: Made and repaired armour and weapons for guards, soldiers and adventurers. Knows steel, leather and how a blade or a plate fails.

name: Tailor
summary: Cut and sewed clothing for townsfolk or nobles. Knows fabric, fashion and the gossip of every customer who came for a fitting.

name: Cook
summary: Cooked for a tavern, a noble kitchen or a garrison. Knows food, spices and how to feed many people on little coin.

name: Innkeeper
summary: Ran or worked in an inn, serving drink, renting rooms and keeping the peace. Hears every rumour that passes along the road.

name: Sailor
summary: Crewed merchant ships or naval vessels along Tamriel's coasts. Knows rigging, ports, storms and the habits of pirates.

name: Shopkeeper
summary: Kept a general store or specialty shop in town, buying cheap and selling dear. Good with numbers and with difficult customers.

name: Peddler
summary: Sold small goods from a pack or cart from village to village. Knows the roads, local prices and a hundred sales tricks.

name: Scholar
summary: Studied history, lore or natural philosophy, perhaps tied to the Arcane University or a learned society. Better with books than with blades.

name: Scribe
summary: Copied books, wrote letters and kept records for a temple, a court or paying clients. Good handwriting and an eye for detail.

name: Imperial clerk
summary: Worked in the Empire's administration, filing records, taxes or petitions. The Nibenese bureaucracy runs on such patient, overlooked people.

name: Alchemist
summary: Brewed potions and poisons from herbs and creature parts. Knows ingredients, their effects and how dangerous a careless mix can be.

name: Apothecary
summary: Ran or worked in a shop selling remedies, ingredients and potions. Part merchant and part healer, trusted by the neighbourhood.

name: Herbalist
summary: Gathered wild plants and fungi to sell to alchemists and healers. Knows the countryside, its plants and its dangers well.

name: Hedge healer
summary: Treated wounds and illness with herbs and simple spells, often for poor folk who could not pay a temple. Practical, steady-handed and calm.

name: Priest or priestess
summary: Served at a chapel or temple, leading prayers, blessing the faithful and giving healing. Knows the gods' teachings and the troubles of a parish.

name: Monastic novice
summary: Lived in a priory or monastery under vows, working, praying and studying. Places like Weynon Priory near Chorrol shelter such quiet brothers.

name: City guard
summary: Kept the peace in a town or city, walking patrols, chasing thieves and guarding gates. Knows the law, the streets and the local troublemakers.

name: Legion soldier
summary: Served in the Imperial Legion, drilling, marching and fighting under Imperial orders. Knows discipline, formations and life in a fort.

name: Mercenary
summary: Sold a sword to whoever paid, from merchants to petty lords. Knows combat and contracts, and that loyalty lasts as long as the coin.

name: Bodyguard
summary: Guarded a wealthy merchant, noble or official from harm. Learned to read a crowd and to stand between a client and a knife.

name: Fighters Guild member
summary: Took contracts through the Fighters Guild: clearing pests, escorting travellers and guarding property. Proud of the guild, wary of rivals.

name: Mages Guild apprentice
summary: Studied magic at a Mages Guild hall, doing chores and lessons in hope of a recommendation to the Arcane University.

name: Enchanter
summary: Bound magic into weapons, armour and jewellery with soul gems. Skilled, well-paid and closely tied to the Mages Guild.

name: Jeweller
summary: Cut gems and worked gold and silver into rings, amulets and fine pieces. Knows stones, value and the people who can afford them.

name: Arena combatant
summary: Fought in the Imperial City Arena for crowds, wagers and fame. Knows showmanship, brutal combat and what it costs to keep winning.

name: Courier
summary: Carried letters and parcels between towns on foot or horseback. Knows the roads, shortcuts and how to keep going in bad weather.

name: Minstrel
summary: Earned coin singing, playing and telling stories in taverns and halls. Knows songs, legends and how to read an audience.

name: Burglar
summary: Broke into houses and shops by night, picking locks and taking what could be sold. Quiet, careful and good at disappearing.

name: Pickpocket
summary: Lifted purses in crowded markets and busy streets. Quick hands, a blank face and a talent for slipping away.

name: Smuggler
summary: Moved untaxed or illegal goods, such as moon sugar and skooma, past guards and customs. Knows hidden coves, bribes and boats.

name: Fence
summary: Bought stolen goods and sold them on quietly. Knows the worth of every item and keeps many secrets on both sides of the law.

name: Beggar
summary: Lived on alms in the streets, watching and listening. In Cyrodiil, beggars are often the eyes and ears of the Thieves Guild.

name: Noble's retainer
summary: Served a noble house as a guard, squire or steward. Knows court life, the household's secrets and how to stay in favour.

name: Household servant
summary: Worked as a maid, cook, valet or footman in a wealthy home. Knows the household's routines and secrets, and how to be unseen.

name: Stablehand
summary: Fed, groomed and cared for horses at a stable or inn. Knows mounts, tack and the travellers who come and go.

name: Shepherd
summary: Watched flocks of sheep or goats on hills and pastures, protecting them from wolves. Patient, outdoorsy and good with animals.

name: Woodcutter
summary: Felled trees and chopped firewood or timber for towns and builders. Strong, practical and used to working alone in the forest.

name: Vintner
summary: Tended vines and made wine, perhaps at one of Skingrad's famous vineyards. Knows grapes, casks and buyers with good taste.

name: Dockworker
summary: Loaded and unloaded ships in a port like Anvil or the Imperial City Waterfront. Strong back, rough friends and knowledge of the docks.
